newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Philippine peso closes strong on inflows.
newsitem.headline: Philippine peso closes strong on inflows.

text.p: The Philippine peso closed strong for the second straight day at 26.363 from 26.365 on the steady inflows of arbitrage money, traders said on Tuesday.

More dollars came in after the Central Bank kept its key overnight borrowing rate at 11.5 percent. The Central Bank had raised its rate by 0.50 percentage points on Monday to counter attacks on the peso due to fears of capital flight from stock market sales.
The peso averaged at 26.362 for the day from 26.367. Market volume was lower at $193 million from $210.8 million.
Traders said the Central Bank bought about $53 million to $65 million in late trade at the rates of 26.361 up to 26.363.
"The important thing now is for the Central Bank to maintain the 11.5 percent rate," a dealer said.
Traders said there could still be an attack on the peso if the Central Bank did not stay firm at 11.5 percent.
